newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour opponents pounce on Meacher tax remarks.
newsitem.headline: UK Labour opponents pounce on Meacher tax remarks.

text.p: Political opponents of Britain's Labour Party on Thursday claimed remarks about tax made by the party's environment spokesman, Michael Meacher, had pointed up the hollowness of the party's pledges not to raise tax rates.

Meacher said in an interview the position was "not as bleak as it seems" after the party's economics spokesman Gordon Brown promised to keep the upper and standard rates of income tax unchanged through the next parliament if Labour came to power.

"He was very careful to exclude other forms of tax. There's capital gains tax, inheritance tax and all the allowances and the share option schemes," Meacher told the left-leaning New Statesman weekly.

Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke told BBC radio that Meacher's comments showed he regarded Brown's promise as "just a device, just to refer to the rates of income tax and plainly collect increased taxation elsewhere".
"Michael Meacher is a spending shadow cabinet member, he intends to spend," Clarke said.

Malcolm Bruce, economics spokesman for the minority Liberal Democrats, accused Brown of hiding the need for higher taxes from the electorate. "It is our contention all along that tax will go up whoever wins the election," he said.
But Labour leader Tony Blair told a London conference the party had always said there must be leeway for a Chancellor of the Exchequer to adjust tax rates in successive budgets.
"What is absolutely untrue, however, is to say that the Labour Party has hidden spending plans which it has not properly financed," he added.
